Accent: Nigerian English. Tone: warm, clear and upbeat, at a steady natural pace.

Transcript:

lines.c_intro: In many lecture halls, students miss what is taught. Voices do not carry, illness keeps them away, or learning itself is hard. Klasync is an assistive platform, so every student can keep up.
lines.s1a: The lecturer signs in and loads the class roster, so attendance is verified against real matric numbers, not a paper register passed around the hall.
lines.s1b: For audio, the lecturer can use the laptop microphone, or a dedicated wireless microphone for big halls, so even the back row hears clearly.
lines.s1c: One tap starts a live session, with a join code and a QR code for the projector.
lines.s2a: Students join on their phones with that code, no account, no app. Captions are light text, not video, so they work even with limited data.
lines.s2b: For students with dyslexia or low vision, the screen adapts: larger text, and a dyslexia-friendly font.
lines.s3: Now the lecture begins. Every word is captioned live, for students who are deaf, hard of hearing, or sitting at the back of the hall.
lines.s4: Students can check in, raise a hand, or send a question. For the shy student, or one far from the lecturer, that is a voice, and the lecturer sees it instantly.
lines.s5: A live summary builds as the lecture runs, so a student who drifts off for a minute, from tiredness or difficulty focusing, can catch up without losing the thread.
lines.s6a: The lecturer can also check understanding on the spot.
lines.s6b: A quick quiz is written from what was just taught. Students answer on their phones, and results arrive live, so the lecturer knows at once whether to move on.
lines.s7: When class ends, attendance is scored automatically, so lecturers can spot students who are slipping away, and reach out in time.
lines.t1: After class is where it matters most. A student who was sick, or stuck in transport, signs in to their archive and finds the whole lecture waiting.
lines.t2: The transcript is searchable and synced to the recording, so they can replay the exact moment they missed, or simply read at their own pace.
lines.t3: Chapters break a long lecture into short parts, so nobody scrubs through two hours to find one idea.
lines.t3b: And the summary gives the key points, a quick refresher before a test.
lines.t4: The concept map shows how ideas connect, which helps visual learners see the big picture. Tap Tour, and it walks through each concept.
lines.t5: For a student who struggles to remember what was taught, from stress, fatigue, or ADHD, flashcards turn the lecture into short practice they can do anywhere.
lines.t6: Then a quiz tests understanding, with instant feedback and an explanation for every answer, so mistakes become learning.
lines.t7: And they can ask the lecture a question. Answers come only from what was said in class, and point to the exact moment.
lines.c_out: Klasync. An assistive platform for inclusive and accessible education.
